newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech amends FCC long-distance filing.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech amends FCC long-distance filing.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said Friday it has filed an additional 1,500 pages of documents with the Federal Communications Commission as part of its application to offer long-distance service from its local-calling region.
The Chicago-based Baby Bell did so after conceding earlier this week that documents were missing in the original filing made on Jan. 2.
The FCC, in response to the new filing, has delayed the 90-day deadline by which the agency must decide on Ameritech's application, moving it to mid-April from early April.

In its original filing, Ameritech submitted more than 4,000 pages of documents to the FCC seeking approval to offer long-distance service from Michigan, making it the first Baby Bell to seek permission for in-region long-distance service under last year's communications law.

An Ameritech spokesman said the amendments mainly cover documents that Michigan regulators will need to determine whether the company has complied with a 14-point checklist showing that it has opened its local network to new rivals.
Under the new timetable, Michigan regulators must give their findings to the FCC on whether to approve or reject the bid by February 6 -- instead of January 22 under the original filing.
The U.S. Justice Department must submit its recommendation to the FCC by February 21, instead of February 6.
